text.p: These are the leading stories in the Mozambican press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

The Mozambican agriculture ministry says there are signs that the south of the country may be hit by drought in the 1997- 1998 crop season, but adds that an accurate forecast will not be possible until the end of September.
- Health authorities in the Mozambican port city of Beira have expressed concern over rabies, which killed five people in the town in the first six months of this year.

- Armed railway police in the Beira Corridor, which links Zimbabwe to the Indian Ocean, say they have the situation under control following a spate of goods train robberies between the towns of Dondo and Mafambisse.
